name: Koteeswarar Temple, Tirukkottaiyur (Kottaiyur)
deity: Shiva as Koteeswarar, with the goddess Pandadu Nayaki
period: Ancient Shaiva shrine of the Chola country, sung by Appar in the Tevaram (7th century); stone temple with medieval and later additions
dynasty: Medieval Tamil patrons (Chola and later; builders not firmly documented)
summary: Koteeswarar Temple at Kottaiyur near Kumbakonam, the Tirukkottaiyur of Appar's hymn, honours a self-manifested linga said to have appeared beneath a castor plant, beside a goddess who plays with a ball.

sections.history: Kottaiyur lies about five kilometres from Kumbakonam on the road to Swamimalai, in the Chola country north of the Kaveri. In the Tevaram it is Tirukkottaiyur, and the saint Appar, also known as Tirunavukkarasar, praised the Lord here in a decad of the Sixth Thirumurai, one that tradition shares between this shrine and the temple at Tiruvalanchuzhi. That hymn makes it a Paadal Petra Sthalam. The name itself carries two memories: koti, a crore, gives the Lord His name Koteeswarar, and kottai, a seed, gives the village its own, Kottaiyur. The stone temple is medieval in character and has been added to over the centuries; its first builders are not firmly documented.
sections.architecture: The most striking feature of the temple is its five-tiered rajagopuram, which announces the shrine from the road. Within, the sanctum holds a self-manifested linga of Koteeswarar, and the goddess Pandadu Nayaki is honoured in her own shrine. Small shrines to Vinayagar and Murugan flank the approach to the sanctum, in the manner of the temples of the Chola country. A sacred spring and tank belong to the temple, and are tied to its legends.
sections.legends: The sthala purana links Kottaiyur to the story of Kumbakonam. Brahma gathered the seeds of all living things, with the Vedas and Puranas, in a pot, the Amrita Kalasam, which drifted on the floodwaters until Shiva, in the guise of a hunter, broke it open with an arrow. Drops of its nectar are said to have fallen at several places, this one among them, though some tellings speak of sandal paste instead. The village name is explained by another tale: the linga was found beneath a castor plant among fallen seeds, and the sage Eranda is remembered here. A prince named Suruchi, son of Sathyarthi, was cursed into a demon's form; he prayed to Shiva, bathed in the temple's spring, and regained his own shape. The goddess's name, Pandadu Nayaki, the lady who plays with a ball, is understood to mean that she tosses aside the sorrows and curses that burden her devotees. Markandeya and the sage Padirayogi are also named among those who worshipped here.
sections.festivals: The most prominent festival is Masi Maham, in February or March, when the deities are taken in procession to the temple tank and offered milk. Margazhi Tiruvathirai, Maha Shivaratri and Panguni Uthiram are kept with devotion, and the arrow festival of Purattasi is also observed. Confirm dates locally, as they follow the Tamil calendar.
sections.experience: Kottaiyur is an easy and rewarding half-day from Kumbakonam. Enter beneath the five-tiered gopuram, bow at the small shrines of Vinayagar and Murugan, and come to the sanctum of Koteeswarar before turning to Pandadu Nayaki. Devotees come to lay down their cares and curses at the feet of the goddess who tosses them away, and many pray for release from long-standing troubles. The temple sits in the calm of a village street, and is quietest in the early morning.

visit.timings: Commonly reported as roughly 6 am to noon and 3 or 4 pm to 8 pm, though published timings vary; confirm locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected: dhotis or trousers for men, sarees, salwar kameez, or long skirts for women, with shoulders and knees covered. Footwear is left at the entrance stands.
visit.photography: Photography is generally permitted in the outer corridors and courtyards but prohibited inside the inner sanctum, in keeping with Tamil Nadu temple rules. Ask temple staff before photographing rituals or priests.
visit.gettingThere: Kottaiyur is in Thanjavur district, about 5 km from Kumbakonam on the Kumbakonam–Swamimalai road. Kumbakonam is the nearest railway station and the usual base for visitors, and Tiruchirappalli has the nearest major airport. Local buses and autorickshaws serve the route.
